record.chaining: This is the write-gated archetype the round-2 brief names: the gate is not money or a card, it is an SEO asset. 'We're mainly looking for websites with good SEO value.' You cannot multiply it without multiplying indexed domains, which is a different resource than storage.
record.limits_note: 1 TB per VDS; disqualification is losing the backlink. Application reviewed for SEO value.
record.reliability_note: 12+ year provider with a history of these barter offers. The failure mode is that the server is removed when the link is removed, not a technical fault.

evidence.proved: '128GB DDR5 RAM / 1TB NVMe SSD / 16 CPU Cores @ 5GHz'; 'You get this high-spec DDoS Protected VDS at no cost. All we ask in return is a backlink to your website.'

card.summary: EUR 5.00/month for Starter: 1 CPU core at 4 GHz and above, 1 GB DDR5, 20 GB NVMe, 1 Gb/s port, 10 TB monthly transfer, Linux, in Europe, US and Asia. Footnot...

free_tier.stated: EUR 5.00/month for Starter: 1 CPU core at 4 GHz and above, 1 GB DDR5, 20 GB NVMe, 1 Gb/s port, 10 TB monthly transfer, Linux, in Europe, US and Asia. Footnoted: Dallas transfer is 10% of the printed value, so the Dallas Starter is 1 TB a month; Singapore, India and Australia ports are 200 Mbps and their base cost is twice the standard rate. Next plans: Developer EUR 10.00 (2 cores, 2 GB, 20 GB, 20 TB), Production EUR 20.00 (3 cores, 3 GB, 60 GB, 30 TB), Business EUR 40.00 (4 cores, 4 GB, 80 GB, 60 TB), Professional EUR 60.00 (8 cores, 8 GB, 120 GB, 70 TB), Enterprise EUR 80.00 (12 cores, 12 GB, 160 GB, 80 TB), Ultimate EUR 100.00 (16 cores, 16 GB, 200 GB, 100 TB).

egress.terms: 10 TB a month on Starter, 20 TB on Developer and 30 TB on Production; Dallas is 10% of the printed value, so 1 TB on Starter. No overage price is stated
egress.free_allowance: 10 TB per month, 1 TB in Dallas

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.tooling: the page documents a VPS control panel with 'unlimited OS reinstalls', real-time resource monitoring and off-site remote backups downloadable from the panel; no API is mentioned on the page read
record.chaining: EUR 5.00 for 1 GB with 10 TB of transfer is the cheapest published transfer among evaluated providers, beating AlexHost's EUR 6.00 on a port a hundred times faster; the Dallas location drops to 1 TB, so this is a buy-transfer provider only outside Dallas, and it is the obvious host for a crawler whose cost is bandwidth rather than disk.

limits.value: 10 TB a month generally, but 1 TB in Dallas, which is the location the tracker's cheapest row names; the allowance therefore depends on which of the fifteen locations the order is placed in. Footnotes also cut Singapore, India and Australia to 200 Mbps and double their base cost, so the cheapest region and the fastest region are not the same one.

record.notes: The tracker's Dallas row of 1,000 GB/month looked like a print error against the vendor's 10 TB until the vendor's footnote 2 explained it as 10% for wholesale cost; the two sources agree and the footnote is the reason, which is why this record states both numbers rather than one. No storage product line exists: storage/evolution-host already records fails-egress for that question on the same catalogue. json, a different provider. verification criteria: whether Dallas is the cheapest location once the 10% cut is applied, and whether the 4 GHz floor is a guarantee or a fleet description.
